---
params:
  x: NULL
  title: "LAGO optimization report"
title: "`r params$title`"
date: "`r format(Sys.time(), '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')`"
output:
  html_document:
    self_contained: true
    mathjax: null
    theme: cosmo
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
x <- params$x
# lago_blocks() is the shared presentation formatter; the report renders from
# the same blocks as print.lago()/summary.lago() so the two can never drift.
# It is an internal helper, hence the triple-colon access.
blocks <- LAGOtrials:::lago_blocks(x)

# The interactive plots are drawn client-side by the vendored D3 v7 library and
# inst/js/lago-report.js, both inlined below, and are fed a JSON payload built
# with jsonlite. jsonlite is a Suggests-only dependency; lago_report() guards
# it, but gate on it here too so rendering the template directly degrades to the
# static plot rather than erroring when jsonlite is absent.
have_jsonlite <- requireNamespace("jsonlite", quietly = TRUE)

# The labels that line up with rec_int and the confidence-set component columns:
# with interaction terms these are the main components (rec_int / cs hold main
# effects only), otherwise the intervention components. Mirrors plot.lago().
plot_components <- if (!is.null(x$display_components)) {
  x$display_components
} else {
  x$intervention_components
}
n_plot_comp <- length(plot_components)
cs_present <- !is.null(x$cs)

# Render the confidence set interactively (D3) for a 1- or 2-component
# intervention when jsonlite is available. When it is not, fall back to the
# static plot.lago() figure for the same 1-/2-component case. For 3+ components
# plot.lago() draws nothing, so neither section appears (matching the static
# report's prior behaviour) and rendering never errors.
interactive_cs <- have_jsonlite && cs_present && n_plot_comp %in% 1:2
static_cs <- cs_present && !interactive_cs && n_plot_comp %in% 1:2

# Cost curves are always drawable (cost_list_of_vectors and the bounds are
# always carried), so the cost section shows whenever jsonlite is available.
interactive_cost <- have_jsonlite &&
  !is.null(x$cost_list_of_vectors) &&
  !is.null(x$intervention_lower_bounds) &&
  !is.null(x$intervention_upper_bounds)

# Build the single JSON payload the client-side D3 code consumes. I() forces
# length-1 vectors (a single-component result) to stay JSON arrays under
# auto_unbox, and digits = NA keeps full numeric precision. cs is emitted
# row-wise as an array of point objects.
report_json <- NULL
if (have_jsonlite) {
  report_data <- list(
    components = I(as.character(plot_components)),
    rec_int = I(as.numeric(x$rec_int)),
    rec_int_cost = as.numeric(x$rec_int_cost),
    cs = x$cs,
    cost = list(
      # Label the cost curves with the same components the cost vectors are
      # indexed by: cost_list_of_vectors and the bounds are per MAIN component,
      # so with interaction terms plot_components (= display_components =
      # main_components) is the aligned, backtick-free label set, not
      # x$intervention_components (which is longer and carries the backticked
      # interaction terms). Identical to intervention_components without them.
      components = I(as.character(plot_components)),
      coefs = lapply(x$cost_list_of_vectors, function(v) I(as.numeric(v))),
      lb = I(as.numeric(x$intervention_lower_bounds)),
      ub = I(as.numeric(x$intervention_upper_bounds))
    )
  )
  report_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
    report_data,
    auto_unbox = TRUE,
    dataframe = "rows",
    na = "null",
    digits = NA
  )
}
```

```{r assets, results='asis', eval=have_jsonlite}
# Inline the vendored D3 v7 library and the report's D3 code directly into the
# HTML (their file CONTENTS inside <script> tags, NOT a <script src=...> link)
# so the output is a single self-contained file with no external asset
# references. The JSON payload is stored once in a global the render calls read.
d3_path <- system.file("js", "d3.v7.min.js", package = "LAGOtrials")
rpt_path <- system.file("js", "lago-report.js", package = "LAGOtrials")
cat("<script>\n")
cat(readLines(d3_path, warn = FALSE), sep = "\n")
cat("\n</script>\n")
cat("<script>\n")
cat(readLines(rpt_path, warn = FALSE), sep = "\n")
cat("\n</script>\n")
cat("<script>\nvar LAGO_REPORT_DATA = ", report_json, ";\n</script>\n", sep = "")
```

```{r inputs, results='asis', eval=!is.null(blocks$inputs)}
cat("## ", blocks$inputs$title, "\n\n", sep = "")
cat(paste0("- ", blocks$inputs$rows), sep = "\n")
```

## `r blocks$recommendation$title`

```{r recommendation}
rec_rows <- blocks$recommendation$rows
if (!is.null(rec_rows$component)) {
  knitr::kable(
    rec_rows,
    col.names = c("Component", "Value"),
    align = c("l", "r")
  )
} else {
  knitr::kable(
    rec_rows,
    col.names = "Value",
    align = "r"
  )
}
```

```{r model, eval=!is.null(x$model)}
# the fitted outcome model carried on the object, shown as its coefficient
# table (same as summary(x$model) in the console summary()).
knitr::kable(
  stats::coef(summary(x$model)),
  caption = "Outcome model coefficients"
)
```

```{r cs-plot-interactive, results='asis', eval=interactive_cs}
# Interactive D3 confidence-set plot (2-component scatter or 1-component strip).
# The recommended intervention is highlighted and each grid point has a hover
# read-out of its component values, cost, and CI bounds.
cat("## Confidence set plot\n\n")
cat(
  '<div id="lago-cs-plot" style="width:100%;max-width:760px;"></div>\n',
  '<script>LAGOReport.renderConfidenceSet("lago-cs-plot",',
  " LAGO_REPORT_DATA);</script>\n",
  sep = ""
)
```

```{r cs-plot-static, eval=static_cs, fig.width=7, fig.height=5, results='asis'}
# Static fallback used only when jsonlite is unavailable: the same
# 1-/2-component confidence-set figure that plot.lago() draws.
cat("## Confidence set plot\n\n")
plot(x)
```

```{r cost-curves, results='asis', eval=interactive_cost}
# Interactive D3 cost curves: for each intervention component, the total-cost
# curve and its derivative (marginal cost), each with a hover read-out. The
# curves use the cost functions the optimization actually ran with.
cat("## Cost functions\n\n")
cat(
  "The total-cost curve and its marginal (per-unit) cost for each ",
  "intervention component, over the component's optimization range. ",
  "Hover a curve to read its value.\n\n",
  sep = ""
)
cat(
  '<div id="lago-cost-curves" style="width:100%;"></div>\n',
  '<script>LAGOReport.renderCostCurves("lago-cost-curves",',
  " LAGO_REPORT_DATA);</script>\n",
  sep = ""
)
```
